clue.text: Chap that adheres to the standard theory of over-promotion

indicators.note: sticking to the next piece, so the two words are joined end to end

parts.note: a chap is any man, here given a common man's name, Peter
a standard is a principle one lives by

explanation.surface: A man who sticks rigidly to the accepted theory about people being promoted beyond their competence.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence J. Peter's well-known theory holds that employees rise until they reach their level of incompetence, a satirical account of over-promotion.

clue.text: Listened in to experimental reggae with Di

indicators.note: an experimental version is a trial arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdropped on a new reggae track made with Di.
explanation.walkthrough: 'experimental' rearranges REGGAE, W and DI together.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is informal British slang for eavesdropping, so the past tense means overheard or listened in.

clue.text: The number of this clue, somehow

definitions.note: read as 'numb-er': something that numbs, an anaesthetic

indicators.note: done in some unknown way, signalling that these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the clue sits at number 3 in the grid, so its number is three

explanation.surface: A puzzle that teasingly points to its own clue number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' does double duty: it is the clue's position (three) and, read as something that numbs, the definition. The indicator rearranges THREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early general anaesthetic, a substance that numbs, so it is a 'numb-er'.

clue.text: First soldier put in position

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
to mount something is to set it in place, as a picture or a gun

explanation.surface: The first soldier was placed at his post.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme or chief, so foremost in importance.

clue.text: Sugarcoating the description of my musical interest

indicators.note: how the setter would describe it in speech, taken as the spoken words that match the entry

parts.note: the setter describing a hobby of singing would say 'I sing'

explanation.surface: Someone making their musical hobby sound sweeter than it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I sing' spoken sounds just like the entry; 'the description of' is the only signal that the words are heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating on a cake, so it is literally a sugarcoating.

clue.text: Final exercise involved with following lawmen around eatery

indicators.note: the agency's letters go round the rest

parts.note: the CIA, the US intelligence agency, loosely taken as lawmen

indicators.note: tangled up together, so these letters are rearranged
only the last letter of exercise is taken

parts.note: following means coming after

explanation.surface: After a last workout, someone is mixed up with police who surround a diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' makes AFETER. Calling the CIA, an intelligence agency, 'lawmen' is a loose stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant, one kind of eatery.

clue.text: Llandudno repertory company welcomes back former president

indicators.note: the run of letters is read in the opposite direction
the words take in a run of letters spanning them

explanation.surface: A theatre company in Llandudno, a Welsh seaside town, hosts a returning ex-president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' finds NOREP across llandudNO REPertory; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Juan Perón was three times President of Argentina.

clue.text: Soon to refurbish general store (rates unknown)

indicators.note: refurbishing remakes the shop, so its letters are rearranged
the letters of rates are absent from the rearranged result

explanation.surface: A village shop is about to be done up, with its business rates not yet known.
explanation.walkthrough: GENERAL STORE holds the letters of RATES plus the answer; 'unknown' removes RATES and 'to refurbish' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ere long is an old-fashioned phrase meaning before long, shortly.

clue.text: Exhibitionist will oppose urbane intervention

indicators.note: the letters come between the ends of the two words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A show-off promises to resist a smooth person's interference.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur behaves affectedly to impress others, a kind of show-off.

clue.text: Pointless work hard for celebrity

indicators.note: without a compass point, here E for east, which is removed

parts.note: an opera is a musical work
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that working hard is futile for someone famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' strips E, a compass point, from OPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Oprah Winfrey, the American talk-show host, is a famous celebrity.

clue.text: Stay in favour of church supplement

parts.note: to stay is to check or restrain, as with a rein
for means supporting
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone stays on in support of a church's additional fund.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to strengthen by adding more, so to supplement or bolster.

clue.text: Satirical piece on English farm animals

parts.note: a pig is one farm animal
a ram is another farm animal

explanation.surface: A satire written about English livestock, like Orwell's Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty saying or poem, often satirical in tone.

clue.text: Become absorbed with negotiators working without Rosa

indicators.note: put to work in a new arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled
the letters of Rosa are taken away from the mix

explanation.surface: Getting involved with negotiators who are operating minus a colleague called Rosa.
explanation.walkthrough: NEGOTIATORS holds the answer plus ROSA; 'without' removes ROSA and 'working' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To get into a hobby or book is to become engrossed in it.

clue.text: Proper Conservative

definitions.meaning: politically on the conservative side, as opposed to the left

explanation.surface: A correct and decent Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both correct and, politically, belonging to the conservative wing.

clue.text: Well-turned-out pottery with special embellishments

parts.note: trim means neat and smart in appearance
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain

explanation.surface: Smart china decorated with special ornamentation.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimmings are decorative additions, as on clothing or a roast dinner.

clue.text: Intimidating artilleryman, good finally, drinking wine

indicators.note: taking in, so the wine goes inside
that letter is shifted to the end of the word

parts.note: a gunner serves in the artillery
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A frightening gunner who, in the end, has been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' moves the G of good to the end, making UNNERG, and 'drinking' takes in the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnerving takes away one's courage, so it is intimidating.

clue.text: Insignificant measure manufactured not near me

indicators.note: made up, so the letters are reassembled into something new

explanation.surface: A tiny unit, made somewhere far from the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanometre is a billionth of a metre, a minute unit of length.

clue.text: Lover, but to Marian a stranger

indicators.note: read as 'more strange', so these letters are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A sweetheart who is nonetheless unknown to Marian.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover or sweetheart, from Italian.

clue.text: Game given wicked new leg

parts.note: bad means evil
mint means brand new, as in mint condition
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A wicked newcomer is handed a fresh leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket game played with a shuttlecock.

clue.text: Spouted rubbish, told stories and was browbeaten

indicators.note: spoken out, so the word for rubbish is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense
lied means told untruths

explanation.surface: A sequence: someone talked nonsense, told fibs, and got pushed around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spouted' makes BULL a sound, written BUL so that LIED supplies the second L. The definition is loose: the answer means intimidated rather than was intimidated.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bullied is being browbeaten or intimidated by someone stronger.

clue.text: President has since invited mother in …

indicators.note: asked in, so the mother goes inside

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it was late'
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A president has had his mother over ever since, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were both US presidents.

clue.text: Fishy? Time will tell!

indicators.note: the letters will tell their story once rearranged, signalling an anagram

parts.note: the word itself supplies the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something seems suspicious, but only time will reveal the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: 'will tell' rearranges FISHY with T for time, describing something suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifty means evasive and untrustworthy, which is what something suspicious seems.

clue.text: … with material she's collected for railway worker

indicators.note: gathered up inside, so one goes within the other

parts.note: linen is a cloth
she refers back to the mother of the previous clue, so MA

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the mother brings the fabric she's gathered for a man on the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineman maintains railway or telegraph lines, a railway worker.

clue.text: Specialised, like opening hours in French resort …

indicators.note: in here means sitting inside the resort's name, so the hour letter goes within it

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

indicators.note: the start of hours, so its first letter

explanation.surface: A specialist note about the opening times of a resort in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche product or market serves a small specialised group.

clue.text: … where early start is welcomed by relative

indicators.note: taken inside, so the letter goes within the resort

parts.note: points back to the French resort in the previous clue

indicators.note: only the beginning of early is used

explanation.surface: A place where an early arrival is welcomed by a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 23: 'where' means the French resort named there.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family relative.

clue.text: Italian visits Ulster scientist

indicators.note: the man comes to Ulster, so the two sit side by side

parts.note: Marco is a typical Italian man's name
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: An Italian scientist makes a trip to Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi, the Italian pioneer of radio, was a physicist and inventor.

clue.text: It shows something up one way or another

indicators.note: the word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something that reveals objects in the sky, from whichever side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' hints at aircraft overhead, which the screen reveals.
explanation.definitionFit: This detection system reveals the position of distant objects such as aircraft on a screen.

clue.text: Working together, still burying shell (almost)

indicators.note: the motionless word goes round the shell

parts.note: inert means motionless

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a conch is a large seashell

explanation.surface: People cooperate while quietly burying a seashell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' removes the H; 'burying' puts the shortened shell inside the word for still.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting jointly, in coordination.

clue.text: Early form of conscription

definitions.meaning: a first version of a document
compulsory enlistment, chiefly in American usage

explanation.surface: A first version of a call-up scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a preliminary version of writing and, in the US, compulsory military service.

clue.text: Practice doctor Les unlikely to block A Shearer's treatment

indicators.note: to stand round and hem in, so one group surrounds the other
in an unlikely form, so these letters are rearranged
given a working over, so these letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: A medic named Les is unlikely to stop a footballer's therapy session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlikely' makes ESL and 'treatment' makes SREHEARSA; 'to block' wraps the first round the second. Alan Shearer is a former England footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: A final full run-through before a performance is a practice session.
